Evaluate an expression without stopping on an error

Source: R/capture.R
capture.Rd

capture() evaluates an expression once and returns its result. If the expression errors, it reports why evaluation did not complete and returns NULL invisibly. Use quiet = TRUE to suppress the failure message.

Usage

capture(x, quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

x

An expression to evaluate once.

quiet

If TRUE, suppress warnings and messages from x and the failure message from capture(). Printed output and the returned value are unchanged. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

The expression's result, preserving its visibility, class and attributes. On error, NULL invisibly.

Details

When updating an existing object, put the assignment inside capture(): capture(data <- update(data)). Writing data <- capture(update(data)) overwrites data with NULL if the update fails.

Like Stata's capture, this lets a script continue after an error. Unlike Stata's command, it returns the successful value, keeps printed output and reports a caught error as a message by default. The failure notice is not a formal R warning and does not become an error under options(warn = 2). Warnings and messages from x propagate unless quiet = TRUE; suppressing them does not stop evaluation. With options(warn = 2), an unsuppressed warning from x becomes an error and is caught. User interrupts are not caught.

A successful FALSE, NA, NULL or object inheriting from try-error is returned unchanged. A successful NULL and a caught error have the same value. Use tryCatch() when you need to distinguish them programmatically or retain the error object. This function no longer returns a success/failure flag, so do not use it as the condition in if (capture(...)).

An assignment inside capture() updates its target only after the right-hand side succeeds. A successful NULL is still assigned. A block of separate assignments retains the last completed update and skips steps after the first error, as Stata's capture blocks do. A single assignment around a pipeline retains its original target on error; intermediate pipeline results are not saved.

Earlier effects are not rolled back. In particular, changes by reference (such as data.table updates) and printed output before an error remain. Invalid quiet values raise an error before x is evaluated.

See also

Other utility functions: set_seed(), timer()

Examples

capture(mean(1:10))
#> [1] 5.5

# Keep a successful result while suppressing warnings and messages
capture({
  message("Calculating")
  mean(1:10)
}, quiet = TRUE)
#> [1] 5.5

# A new object receives NULL on error, with a failure message
result <- capture(stop("Cannot calculate"))
#> Captured expression did not complete.
#> i Reason: Cannot calculate
#> i Earlier changes, if any, were not undone.

# An existing object is kept if its replacement fails
data <- tibble::tibble(x = 1:3)
capture(data <- dplyr::mutate(data, y = x * 2))
capture(data <- stop("Update failed"))
#> Captured expression did not complete.
#> i Reason: Update failed
#> i Earlier changes, if any, were not undone.
data
#> # A tibble: 3 x 2
#>       x     y
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1     1     2
#> 2     2     4
#> 3     3     6

# Separate assignments keep the last completed update
capture({
  data <- dplyr::mutate(data, z = x + 1)
  data <- stop("Second update failed")
  data <- dplyr::mutate(data, later = TRUE)
})
#> Captured expression did not complete.
#> i Reason: Second update failed
#> i Earlier changes, if any, were not undone.
data
#> # A tibble: 3 x 3
#>       x     y     z
#>   <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1     2     2
#> 2     2     4     3
#> 3     3     6     4

# A single assignment keeps the original target if any pipeline step fails
capture(data <- data |>
  dplyr::mutate(temporary = x * 10) |>
  dplyr::mutate(failed = stop("Pipeline failed")))
#> Captured expression did not complete.
#> i Reason: i In argument: `failed = stop("Pipeline failed")`. Caused by error: !
#>   Pipeline failed
#> i Earlier changes, if any, were not undone.
data
#> # A tibble: 3 x 3
#>       x     y     z
#>   <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1     2     2
#> 2     2     4     3
#> 3     3     6     4
